r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped service dependencies around auth-service, mobile-bff, and redis-session, and collected all deployments, config changes, and infrastructure changes within the 7-day window. Identified key changes including auth-service deploy v7.2.0 on Oct 14, mobile-bff deploy v7.19.8 on Oct 15, and a kubernetes node pool infra change involving time sync at 13:36:00 UTC on Oct 16, just minutes before the reported incident onset at ~13:40 UTC.

findings.statement: mobile-bff sync calls auth-service, payments-api, portfolio-service, orders-service, kyc-service, and aa-connector.
auth-service sync calls user-db, redis-session, and otp-provider.
auth-service was deployed to version v7.2.0 (session refresh UX) on 2026-10-14T16:00:00+00:00.
mobile-bff was deployed to version v7.19.8 (minor bug fixes) on 2026-10-15T01:03:00+00:00.

An infrastructure change on kubernetes node pool np-3 (new node image 2026.10.3, time sync: chrony -> systemd-timesyncd) occurred at 2026-10-16T13:36:00+00:00, four minutes prior to the incident report onset (~13:40).

open_questions: Did the kubernetes node image update (chg-9296) involving time-sync changes affect token/session validation or expiration checks in auth-service or redis-session?
Was the auth-service v7.2.0 release (chg-8214) exhibiting delayed bugs related to session handling after OTP verification?

r1-observability-1.summary: Logins failed with session invalid errors starting exactly at 2026-10-16T13:40:00+00:00. auth-service error rate jumped to over 30% due to JWT validation failures regarding future-issued tokens (iat skew), while mobile-bff experienced a matching increase in error rate and received 401 status responses from auth-service.

findings.statement: auth-service error rate spiked from baseline 0.28% to 32.36% at 2026-10-16T13:40:00+00:00.
mobile-bff error rate spiked from baseline 0.32% to 5.93% at 2026-10-16T13:40:00+00:00.
auth-service began logging JWT validation errors due to iat skew starting at 2026-10-16T13:40:09+00:00.
mobile-bff began logging 401 responses from auth-service for POST /v1/session starting at 2026-10-16T13:40:18+00:00.
Neither auth-service nor mobile-bff experienced pod restarts or CPU/memory saturation during the incident onset.

open_questions: What caused the time synchronization drift or clock skew on node np-3-a1 resulting in future-issued tokens?

r2-observability-1.summary: Investigation of kubernetes node pool np-3 confirms that a node image update at 13:36 on 2026-10-16 changed time synchronization from chrony to systemd-timesyncd, resulting in clock desynchronization and a clock offset of ~99 seconds on node np-3-a1 starting at 13:39.

findings.statement: kubernetes node pool np-3 was updated with new node image 2026.10.3 at 13:36 on 2026-10-16, switching time sync from chrony to systemd-timesyncd.
Kubernetes emits no numerical metrics, only events and logs.
Kubernetes logs began showing clock synchronization warnings on node np-3-a1 starting at 13:39:27, showing a clock offset of +99s exceeding the 5s threshold.
Clock offset warnings on node np-3-a1 persisted continuously between 91s and 99s throughout the investigation window.

hypotheses.title: Node image update time-sync configuration shift causes clock skew and JWT iat validation failure
hypotheses.mechanism: An infrastructure node pool patch (chg-9296) changed time synchronization from chrony to systemd-timesyncd on node pool np-3 at 13:36:00 UTC, causing node np-3-a1 to drift by +99s. When auth-service pods running on this node attempted to validate incoming JWTs, their local system clock appeared ahead of the token issuance time, triggering JWT validation errors due to 'token issued in the future (iat skew 97s)' starting at 13:40:00 UTC.

supporting.note: Infrastructure update changing time sync method occurred at 13:36:00 UTC, four minutes prior to the incident onset.
Kubernetes node log explicitly shows clock offset +99s on node np-3-a1 starting at 13:39:27.
auth-service pod on node np-3-a1 explicitly logged JWT validation failure due to iat skew starting at 13:40:09 UTC.
auth-service error rate spiked sharply from 0.28% to over 30% starting at 13:40:00 UTC.
mobile-bff received 401 responses from auth-service starting at 13:40:18 UTC.

assumptions: The change from chrony to systemd-timesyncd caused an abrupt clock step or drift on node np-3-a1 rather than smooth synchronization.

hypotheses.title: Delayed bug in auth-service session refresh release triggered by standard time validation
hypotheses.mechanism: auth-service v7.2.0 deploy introduced strict token validation or session logic that began incorrectly rejecting sessions after OTP verification due to minor clock differences.

supporting.note: auth-service was deployed to version v7.2.0 two days prior to the incident.
auth-service error rate increased dramatically during the incident.

contradicting.note: The incident onset correlates precisely with the time-sync infrastructure change at 13:36:00 UTC rather than the deployment time two days prior.

assumptions: The deployment contained a dormant bug that remained latent until triggered by external environmental factors.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: The symptom onset is established at 2026-10-16T13:40:00+00:00, where auth-service and mobile-bff error rates spiked simultaneously. The direct cause of failure is documented in auth-service logs (log-00613) as JWT iat skew on node np-3-a1. Kubernetes node log (log-00607) explicitly confirms clock desynchronization (+99s offset) on node np-3-a1 starting at 13:39:27, immediately following the infrastructure update (chg-9296) at 13:36:00 UTC. Hypothesis H1 is conclusively supported by direct infrastructure log evidence, addressing the critic's concern regarding kubernetes health verification.
